overall_summary: Analysis of 47 deduplicated shorts shows that extreme exoplanet survival and visceral 'What If You Fell Into...' spatial scenarios dominate channel viewership and engagement (averaging 700-1,050+ views and 3-4% like ratios). Conversely, psychology brain facts and repeated common trivia ('Why Space Is Completely Silent', fake memories, earworms) severely underperform, rarely crossing 100 views. Videos in the 19-21 second range consistently outperform shorter clips under 16 seconds.

winning_patterns.pattern: 'What If You Fell Into [Extreme Cosmic Hazard]' Hook Format
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Darkest Planet?' (824 views, 15 likes) led the channel in total views, likes, and comments.
winning_patterns.action: Use visceral second-person POV 'What if you fell into...' hooks paired with extreme, scientifically verified cosmic phenomena.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet of Burning Ice' (1,057 views), 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' (1,031 views, 36 likes), and 'Supersonic Rubies' (725 views, 25 likes) dramatically outperformed shorter 12-16s videos.
winning_patterns.action: Anchor scripts around high-contrast sensory contradictions (extreme heat/cold, bizarre atmospheres) and pace them tightly across 20-21 seconds.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' was reposted across three variations yielding only 5, 10, and 53 views; 'Brain Is Hiding This From You' gained 38 views.
weak_patterns.action: Halt generic psychology and human memory facts until channel baseline viewership expands.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Why Space Is Completely Silent' posted three times peaked at only 220 views and bottomed at 34 views.
weak_patterns.action: Retire commonly known school-level trivia in favor of exotic, lesser-known deep space or planetary survival scenarios.
